tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Weak maximum principle]1. ch2:2.3\group chapter-2 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0027 Let $\Omega $ be bounded and $u\in C^2(\Omega )\cap C^0(\overline\Omega )$. Then \begin{equation} \tag {2.7} \Delta u\geq 0\Longrightarrow \sup _\Omega u=\sup _{\partial \Omega }u, \qquad \Delta u\leq 0\Longrightarrow \inf _\Omega u=\inf _{\partial \Omega }u. \end{equation} In particular, a harmonic function lies between its boundary extrema.
Proof

↗ gt.thm2.3 \sketch An extremum exists on the compact closure. If it were achieved only in the interior, Theorem 2 would make $u$ constant.
